source: GeoNames (CC BY 4.0) current city ID/coordinates; historical municipal, parliamentary, national archive, UNESCO and government records cited in per-period sourceUrl
selection: 25 distinct P-class capital/government-seat settlements in the Americas not present in batches 1–15. Names do not assign historical city ranks or political borders.
coordinateConvention: Modern GeoNames EPSG:4326 representative points only, not historical sites/boundaries.
countryCodeSemantics: Modern GeoNames sourceCountryCode does not infer historical sovereignty, official language or rank.
coverageNote: A single 1801 period in low-change cities is an editorial baseline, not proof of uninterrupted historical official usage. Unknown transitions remain unresolved; no inferred dates or legal claims.
reviewMethod: Evidence-backed multi-transition capitals separately audited (Ottawa, Santo Domingo, Port-au-Prince, Bogotá, Sucre, Georgetown, Belmopan, Brasília); the remaining period-stable candidates carry a baseline and explicit research limitation.
qualityNotes: All 25 GeoNames IDs are distinct and absent from batches 01–15. The previous 88 city records are untouched.
1991 Bogotá Article 322 restored Santa Fe de Bogotá; 2000 amendment effective 18 August used for Bogotá. 1819-12-17 dropped Santa Fe.

Santo Domingo: original law 1067 published 11 January 1936 and restoration law 5674 promulgated 23 November 1961, per Dominican Senate original expediente 8179; some secondary summaries claim 20 October or 21 November and are not preferred.
Sucre: 12 July 1839 law named city Sucre from Chuquisaca, no backdating to independent state formation.
Georgetown: 5 May 1812 renamed Stabroek urban area as Georgetown; modern Stabroek ward is not identical to historic city object.

Haiti Port-au-Prince: historical studies date Port-Républicain in 1801, restoration 1804, brief re-use 1843 to 1845. Only 1804 name-recovery calendar date is available in the cited scholarly note; later changes year-level.
Belmopan and Brasília are documented modern new cities, with urban eligibility staged from 1970 and 1960-04-21 respectively; city-lifecycle is independent of naming.
Do not treat La Paz's seat-of-government role as constitutional capital of Bolivia; Sucre and La Paz have separate IDs.
Panamá Viejo and the replacement city after 1673 must retain different historical city sites; present GeoNames point is not automatically reused for abandoned old site.

All single-period 1801 cases require future source-by-era verification where greater precision is important. English and native orthography choices are map editorial labels, not evidence that those forms were legally established in 1801.
No PLAC v3 publishing, no runtime, no main or app repository changes.

Each record has researchDifficulty A/B/C. A-class single-period historical continuity is editorial provisional and must not be treated as an independently documented absence of renaming throughout 1801–2026.
